papers.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank penalty to LoRA training. Mixed-domain rank sweeps report lower mean Wiki perplexity than unpenalized LoRA at every tested rank of at least 16 for λ = 0.01, though greater rank utilization does not always help.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses whether spectral regularization can improve low-rank adaptation while preserving learning and retention.

evidence.quote: a penalty weight of λ = 0.01 \\lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA.
Fuller spectral utilization need not improve every perplexity metric, so effective rank should be interpreted jointly with mixture fit and the held-out probes.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Shows that low stable rank can coexist with a broad update spectrum in language-model post-training. Selected OLMo-2-7B PPO attention updates have stable ranks of 9.6–18.3 but need 532–1,222 components for 80% energy.
papers.relevance: Warns against treating stable rank alone as evidence that weight updates are cheaply compressible.

evidence.quote: three proximal policy optimization (PPO) attention updates have stable ranks of 9.6-18.3 but require 532-1,222 singular components to capture 80% of their energy.
Assessing the task-level value of that energy requires evaluating models after spectral truncation.

papers.title: Spectral Rank and Step-Direction Dynamics in Language-Model Post-Training

papers.summary: FOAM reduces SOAP optimizer state through one-sided preconditioning and factored moments. In reported 124M–760M pretraining comparisons, it approaches SOAP validation loss with half SOAP's matrix-parameter state and substantially less wall-clock time.
papers.relevance: Provides measured quality, memory, and time trade-offs for matrix-structured LLM optimization.

evidence.quote: FOAM uses half of SOAP’s matrix-parameter state at every size, and its measured peak memory at small size is + 7.4 % +7.4\\% over AdamW against + 12.9 % +12.9\\% for SOAP.
SOAP attains the lowest validation loss at every scale, with FOAM behind by 0.004 0.004 , 0.008 0.008 , and 0.005 0.005 nats at small, medium, and large, each within about one seed std.

papers.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP

papers.summary: Finds delayed effects of temporary weight decay in Muon pretraining: a schedule transferred from 162M to 1.4B is worse immediately after removal but improves final validation loss relative to no decay and a sampled constant-decay baseline.
papers.relevance: Connects regularization schedules, weight norms, and final model quality across pretraining scales.

evidence.quote: a schedule selected at 162M and transferred without retuning to 1.4B is 0.26 nats worse than no decay when removed, overtakes it only after 73% of training, and ultimately finishes 0.028 nats better while also outperforming the best sampled constant-decay baseline.
these runs do not locate the optimal duration.

papers.summary: HiLo transmits compressed gradients for LoRA post-training while workers replay optimizer updates. Spar's spectral compression keeps training rank 64 and, on two reasoning tasks, approaches full-synchronization accuracy at small communication budgets.
papers.relevance: Directly tests the quality–communication–throughput trade-off without reducing LoRA training rank.

evidence.quote: Low-rank LoRA reduces the training rank to k k , whereas all HiLo variants keep rank 64 and compress only the communicated gradients
On KK at rank 1 (1.6% of the bytes), HiLo + Spar reaches 81.6% pass@4 against 83.2% for Full Sync

papers.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training

papers.summary: SCALAR trains scalar coefficients over fixed directions. On Qwen2.5-7B commonsense fine-tuning, reported accuracy is comparable to rank-8 LoRA with fewer trainable parameters, lower peak memory, and higher throughput.
papers.relevance: Offers a concrete PEFT comparison spanning adaptation quality, parameter budget, memory, and speed.

evidence.quote: At the largest reported coefficient budgets, SCALAR obtains average accuracies of 88.9 on Qwen2.5-7B and 87.3 on LLaMA3-8B, compared with 88.8 and 87.4 for rank-8 LoRA.
SCALAR achieves the lowest peak memory among the evaluated PEFT methods, using 20% less memory than LoRA
Training throughput increases by 6% over LoRA

papers.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

papers.summary: MemCredit learns memory-selection utility from counterfactual interventions, using semantic retrieval for candidate generation and predicted decision utility to allocate context. It outperforms BM25 memory retrieval on ALFWorld under a 500-token budget.
papers.relevance: Suggests a testable context-management design for a research-digest agent, though its evaluations are on other agent tasks.

evidence.quote: semantic relevance retrieves a broad candidate pool, while predicted utility determines which memories are retained under a fixed token budget.
On ALFWorld, MemCredit achieves 86.57 % 86.57\\% SR@50 under a 500-token historical-memory budget, compared with 65.67 % 65.67\\% for BM25 retrieval.

papers.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents

limitations: The spectral-rank paper does not establish task-level quality after truncating updates; its full-SVD validation covers selected matrices.
FOAM's main reported scale comparison is 124M–760M, so frontier-scale behavior remains uncertain.
HiLo's reported speedups depend on bandwidth-constrained links, and its held-out accuracy comparison uses three seeds on two reasoning tasks.
SCALAR's memory and throughput measurements are for Qwen2.5-7B fine-tuning on two NVIDIA H20 GPUs; results need not generalize to other systems.
MemCredit was evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop, not a research-digest workflow.
